L2t: Under contract law, a builder whose client wrongfully repudiates a construction contract is entitled to expectation damages, meant to put the builder in the position full performance would have.
L3t: Expectation damages equal the costs already incurred plus the profit the builder would have made on the contract, reduced by any loss the builder avoided, such as by reselling unused materials.
L4t: The builder recovers $14,000: $10,000 in costs plus $5,000 in expected profit, minus the $1,000 recouped by reselling the materials.
L2f: Courts handle disputes over unfinished construction work by always splitting the loss evenly between the builder and the property owner.
L3f: Because the builder's claim rests on unjust enrichment, the recovery is capped at the benefit the homeowner actually received from the partial work.
L4f: The builder will likely recover only $3,000, the amount by which the partial greenhouse increased the value of the homeowner's property.
